Miami's bar landscape is undergoing a notable transformation as establishments begin featuring vermouth and sherry-based cocktails alongside the rum and agave spirits that have long defined the city's drinking scene. According to Eater Miami, classic Spanish cocktails are increasingly appearing on menus across the city, marking a shift in what Miami drinkers are seeking as the market matures.

For decades, Miami has leveraged its geographic position as a gateway between the U.S., the Caribbean, and Latin America to champion diverse flavors—rum and agave spirits mingling with notes of citrus and exotic fruits have been hallmarks of the local cocktail identity. That foundation remains, but bartenders are now layering in the botanical complexity of vermouth, a fortified wine flavored with various botanicals and produced primarily in Italy, France, and Spain since the 18th century.

The emergence of sherry and vermouth-forward bars reflects a broader aperitivo movement gaining traction among American cocktail enthusiasts. These fortified wines, with their lower alcohol content and sipping-focused preparation, appeal to drinkers looking for an alternative to high-proof spirits. In Miami's context, they also represent a natural extension of the city's existing relationship with Spanish and Mediterranean cuisine and culture.

Miami's sprawling metropolitan area—home to an estimated 6.39 million residents and ranking as the fifth-largest metro area in the Southeast—provides both the population density and the cultural diversity to support specialized bar concepts. These new bar openings suggest that Miami's reputation as a culinary and hospitality destination continues to deepen. The June 19, 2026 edition continues this tradition, pulling together restaurant news, upcoming events, and local food industry developments from across the region.

The format serves a practical purpose for both casual food enthusiasts and industry insiders. Rather than spreading stories across multiple posts throughout the week, the publication consolidates announcements into one digestible package that readers can scan for updates affecting their favorite neighborhoods or dining interests. According to Miami Food Pug, this weekly compilation approach helps ensure that smaller announcements and community events receive visibility alongside major restaurant launches.

South Florida's food scene remains dynamic, with constant movement in the restaurant industry. New establishments open regularly while established venues occasionally close or relocate, and chefs frequently announce new ventures or transitions. Local food events range from popup dinners to chef collaborations to industry gatherings, each offering different experiences for diners and networking opportunities for food professionals.

The roundup format also reflects how local food coverage has evolved in the digital age. Rather than operating on a strictly chronological publishing schedule, food publications increasingly curate and repackage content to help audiences navigate information overload. By grouping related stories together, outlets like Miami Food Pug add editorial value beyond individual news items, helping readers understand broader patterns in the local dining landscape.

For restaurants and food businesses, inclusion in such roundups provides valuable exposure to an engaged audience actively interested in local dining news. The visibility can drive foot traffic to openings, alert customers to events, and help establishments maintain awareness even during quiet news cycles when they might not warrant standalone coverage.

title: Maple & Ash’s Miami Spice 2026, A Decadent Reservation
summary: Maple and Ash Miami is luxe—from the stewardship of its two-star Michelin chef/partner Danny Grant and the contemporary-meets-Old World décor, to the rich ingredients in its menus and very professional service. No surprise then that its Miami Spice 2026 dinner menu would be…
whatHappening: Maple & Ash, a two-star Michelin restaurant in Miami helmed by chef Danny Grant, has unveiled its Miami Spice 2026 dinner menu. The establishment is leveraging the annual dining promotion to showcase its luxury positioning through a curated prix-fixe experience.
whoInvolved: Maple & Ash is a high-end restaurant led by chef and partner Danny Grant, who has earned the restaurant two Michelin stars—a distinction awarded by the Michelin Guide to select restaurants meeting exceptional standards of culinary excellence. The restaurant is participating in Miami Spice, an annual dining initiative that brings elevated menus to the city's restaurant scene.
whyMatters: Miami Spice is a key opportunity for luxury restaurants to attract new diners and reinforce their market position during a designated promotional period. For Maple & Ash, the initiative demonstrates how Michelin-starred establishments use special menus to balance accessibility with their premium brand identity, potentially expanding their customer base while maintaining gastronomic standards.
articleBody:
Maple & Ash in Miami is stepping into the spotlight with its Miami Spice 2026 dinner menu, offering diners a chance to experience the restaurant's distinctive culinary approach at a structured price point. According to Miami Curated, the menu reflects the restaurant's commitment to luxury across every dimension—from its contemporary design infused with Old World aesthetics to its carefully sourced, rich ingredients and fastidious service standards.

The restaurant operates under the stewardship of chef and partner Danny Grant, whose culinary credentials include recognition from the Michelin Guide, the prestigious international reference for dining excellence that has evaluated restaurants since 1900. The Michelin Guide awards up to three stars to select establishments based on evaluations by anonymous inspectors, and Maple & Ash's two-star status places it among a rarified group of restaurants demonstrating exceptional culinary achievement and consistency.

Miami Spice represents a significant moment in the annual dining calendar for Miami's restaurant community. The promotion invites high-end establishments to craft special menus that balance their culinary vision with accessibility to a broader audience. For a restaurant of Maple & Ash's caliber, the initiative serves as both a platform to showcase the kitchen's capabilities and an opportunity to introduce the establishment's philosophy to potential regulars who may not have previously dined there.

The restaurant's approach to its Spice menu underscores a broader philosophy: that luxury dining need not be exclusive in reach, even as it remains uncompromising in execution. The contemporary-meets-Old World design aesthetic that characterizes the physical space extends to the menu itself, which appears to blend classical technique with modern sensibility. Every element—from ingredient selection to service—has been calibrated to deliver an experience consistent with the restaurant's premium positioning.

For diners, the Miami Spice offering from Maple & Ash represents an entry point into a restaurant that has achieved recognition at the highest levels of the culinary world. The special menu format allows patrons to experience Danny Grant's vision within a defined framework, making it an ideal moment for those curious about what distinguishes a two-star Michelin establishment from other fine dining destinations in the region.

title: Miami Spice Back with New Reserve Tier and 300 Restaurants
summary: The 25th edition of Miami Spice Restaurant Months is back from August 1 through September 30, 2026. This year’s program from The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) features three-course prix-fixe menus at a minimum of 30% savings at more than 300 participating…
whatHappening: Miami Spice Restaurant Month is returning for its 25th year, running from August 1 through September 30, 2026. The program now features a new reserve tier and expands participation to more than 300 restaurants offering three-course prix-fixe menus at a minimum of 30% savings.
whoInvolved: The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) oversees the program, a major tourism and hospitality promotion organization for the Miami area. The initiative brings together hundreds of restaurants across the region to participate in the annual dining promotion.
whyMatters: Miami Spice is a marquee culinary tourism event that drives significant foot traffic and revenue to participating restaurants during the slower summer and early fall season. The addition of a reserve tier and expanded restaurant count signals growing demand and allows the program to reach both casual and upscale diners, strengthening Miami's position as a major food destination.
articleBody:
Miami's most anticipated dining event is returning for its 25th edition this summer. According to Miami Curated, Miami Spice Restaurant Month runs from August 1 through September 30, 2026, featuring three-course prix-fixe menus at more than 300 participating restaurants with savings of at least 30 percent off regular prices.

The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) has expanded the program this year with a new reserve tier, allowing the event to cater to a broader spectrum of diners. The tiered structure enables casual dining establishments and fine-dining venues alike to participate, making the promotion accessible across different price points and culinary styles throughout the Miami area.

Miami Spice has long served as a critical promotional tool for the region's hospitality industry, particularly during the traditionally slower summer months. The program drives tourism and encourages both locals and visitors to explore new restaurants and revisit established favorites. The August-to-September window allows restaurants to maintain strong traffic during a period when Miami typically experiences slower tourism due to heat and humidity.

The expanded participation to more than 300 restaurants reflects the growing maturity of Miami's dining scene and the event's increasing relevance to the local food community. Over two decades, Miami Spice has evolved from a smaller initiative into one of the city's most recognized culinary events, rivaling similar programs in other major metropolitan areas.

The addition of a reserve tier represents a strategic shift to segment offerings and appeal to diners seeking premium experiences alongside traditional prix-fixe options. This approach allows high-end establishments to participate without cannibalizing their regular pricing structures, while simultaneously ensuring that neighborhood restaurants and casual concepts can still attract deal-conscious diners.

title: Where Elegance Lives: 5 Wonderful Miami Bars
summary: One of my go-to spots when I’m in New York City is the iconic King Cole Bar at the St. Regis. Stepping inside always feels like an immersion into a bygone era—a time when elegance was a deeply desired way of life. Even as modern fashion has shifted toward the casual, the bar…
whatHappening: Miami Curated has compiled a curated list of five elegant bars in Miami, drawing inspiration from iconic establishments like the King Cole Bar at Manhattan's St. Regis Hotel. The publication explores venues that prioritize sophistication and timeless design in an era increasingly dominated by casual dining culture.
whoInvolved: Miami Curated is the source behind this bar guide. The article references the King Cole Bar at the St. Regis New York, a Forbes five-star, AAA five-diamond luxury hotel located at 2 East 55th Street in Midtown Manhattan, originally completed in 1904 and currently operated by Marriott International.
whyMatters: As casual fashion and dining culture increasingly dominates consumer preferences, establishments that maintain formal elegance and refined atmospheres offer an alternative for patrons seeking a return to sophisticated hospitality. This curated guide helps Miami visitors and residents discover venues that preserve the aesthetic and experiential values associated with classic luxury establishments.
articleBody:
Miami Curated has released a guide highlighting five exceptional bars across Miami that exemplify elegance and refined hospitality. The publication's approach draws clear inspiration from iconic establishments like the King Cole Bar at the St. Regis New York, where stepping inside feels like entering a different era—one in which elegance was not merely an aesthetic choice but a deeply desired way of life.

The King Cole Bar itself stands as a touchstone for classic luxury. Located at the St. Regis New York on Fifth Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, the hotel was originally developed by John Jacob Astor IV and completed in 1904 by architectural firm Trowbridge & Livingston. Today, operating under Marriott International, the property maintains its Forbes five-star and AAA five-diamond ratings, a testament to its enduring commitment to refined service and design.

According to Miami Curated, the five Miami bars selected for this guide capture a similar philosophy—maintaining standards of elegance even as modern fashion and culture have shifted decisively toward the casual. The publication reports that each venue reflects a commitment to creating immersive experiences rooted in timeless design principles and sophisticated service.

The tension between casual modernity and classical elegance forms the backdrop for this curated selection. While contemporary culture increasingly embraces relaxed dress codes and informal dining, these Miami establishments represent spaces where guests can still experience hospitality executed with the precision and attention to detail associated with luxury establishments of earlier decades.

For Miami visitors and residents seeking bars that prioritize atmosphere and refinement over trendiness, the guide offers a roadmap to venues that maintain the standards exemplified by icons like the King Cole Bar. Each selection balances historical authenticity with contemporary comfort, creating spaces where elegance remains not a nostalgic affectation but an active principle of operation.

articleBody:

title: From Casual Lunch to Serious Dinner: Paperfish Sushi Brickell Stepped Up Its Game
summary: Paperfish Sushi Brickell has always been one of my “go to” places to have lunch or happy hour with a friend and they always like it. With all of the sushi restaurants in town you’d ask why Paperfish Sushi? The lovely décor that brightens up your day the moment you walk in,…
whatHappening: Paperfish Sushi Brickell has elevated its offerings from a casual lunch and happy hour destination to a serious dinner establishment. The restaurant is drawing renewed attention for combining its signature welcoming décor with an expanded dining experience.
whoInvolved: Paperfish Sushi Brickell is a sushi restaurant located in Brickell, Miami's financial district neighborhood situated east of Interstate 95 and south of the Central Business District. The establishment has built a reputation as a reliable go-to spot for casual diners and professionals in the area.
whyMatters: The restaurant's expansion into the dinner market reflects a strategic response to Miami's competitive sushi landscape, where differentiation matters for sustained success. For Brickell's business district, which sees significant weekday foot traffic, a strengthened dining venue adds to the neighborhood's appeal beyond working hours.
articleBody:
Paperfish Sushi Brickell has long served as a reliable refuge for lunch breaks and after-work gatherings, a place where colleagues and friends could count on a pleasant experience without pretense. But the restaurant is now making a bid to capture the dinner crowd as well, signaling confidence in its ability to compete at a higher level. According to Miami Curated, the establishment has "stepped up its game," suggesting meaningful changes to how it presents itself and its offerings during evening hours.

Brickell, Miami's financial district, has historically been defined by its business-focused character, located directly east of Interstate 95 and north of Coconut Grove. The neighborhood's identity as the economic engine of South Florida means that restaurants here must cater to diverse needs—from quick business lunches to more leisurely evenings. Paperfish appears to be recognizing this opportunity.

The restaurant's longstanding appeal has rested partly on factors beyond the food itself. The article notes that the "lovely décor that brightens up your day" creates an inviting atmosphere the moment patrons walk through the door. This aesthetic foundation gives the restaurant a base on which to build a more refined dinner concept without sacrificing the approachability that made it successful during lunch hours.

In a sushi market crowded with options across Miami, Paperfish's move to emphasize its dinner service represents a calculated effort to stand out. Rather than compete solely on price or novelty, the restaurant is leaning on its existing strengths—pleasant surroundings and customer loyalty—and amplifying them for an evening audience that may expect more from the experience.

For regular patrons who have treated Paperfish as a casual spot, the restaurant's evolution offers something new without abandoning what made it work in the first place. The question now is whether this expanded ambition will resonate with Brickell diners seeking a more serious sushi experience.

title: New Places to Shop, Eat in the Miami Design District
summary: With the crowds having gone from the Dolce & Gabbana show and many from FIFA, now is a good time to make a visit to the Miami Design District, especially since new shops have opened that are brands that are probably new to you as well as restaurants. Plus, you might come across…
whatHappening: The Miami Design District is experiencing a wave of new retail and dining openings as major events like the Dolce & Gabbana fashion show and FIFA conclude. The neighborhood is capitalizing on the post-event lull to attract visitors to its fresh crop of brands and restaurants.
whoInvolved: Dolce & Gabbana, the Italian luxury fashion house founded in 1985, held a major show in the area. The Miami Design District itself—a established shopping and cultural hub home to over 130 galleries, showrooms, and luxury retailers—is the focal point of this expansion.
whyMatters: New retail and dining options strengthen the Design District's appeal as a year-round destination beyond major events. The timing gives locals and tourists a chance to discover emerging brands and establishments when crowds have thinned, making for a more relaxed shopping experience.
articleBody:
The Miami Design District is poised for a retail and dining refresh, with several new establishments opening their doors as the neighborhood bounces back from hosting major events. With crowds dispersing after the Dolce & Gabbana show and FIFA activities winding down, the district is an opportune destination for visitors seeking to discover fresh shopping and dining experiences, according to Miami Curated.

The Miami Design District has long established itself as a premier shopping, dining, and cultural destination in Miami, Florida. The neighborhood is home to over 130 art galleries, showrooms, creative services, architecture firms, luxury fashion stores, antiques dealers, and eateries and bars. This diversity of offerings has made it a magnet for both locals and tourists seeking curated retail and cultural experiences.

The latest expansion adds to this existing ecosystem with new brands that many visitors may encounter for the first time, alongside novel restaurants that promise to enhance the neighborhood's already robust dining scene. The influx of new openings reflects ongoing investment in the district and its evolution as a destination that attracts both high-profile fashion events and everyday shoppers.

The timing of these openings is particularly strategic. Following major events like the Dolce & Gabbana presentation and FIFA activities, the district offers a calmer environment for visitors to explore at leisure. Rather than navigating crowds drawn by marquee events, visitors can discover these new establishments and take advantage of the neighborhood's 130-plus galleries, showrooms, and existing retailers without the typical event-day congestion.

For the Design District, these openings underscore the neighborhood's continued relevance as a dynamic retail and cultural hub. Whether visitors come for the new shops and restaurants or to explore the established galleries and luxury brands, the district's appeal extends well beyond any single event.
